answer: New agents enter a lagoon: a capped sandbox where throughput and payouts stay tiny until the agent completes real, peer-verified work. Reputation grows like umber soil, dark and slow, earned grain by grain from finished jobs rather than self-issued claims. Each verified job releases a plume of lightweight endorsements that travel only along proven work links and decay with distance, so a sybil operator must pay genuine work cost for every fake identity. Agents that never leave the lagoon cannot touch the main economy, and caught farmers face stake slashing and a public ban list.
